title: Microsoft Viva: targeted audience surveys in the Copilot Dashboard
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft supports the default, rollout windows, audience behaviour and controls, including the dashboard's survey-data licensing threshold. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting Pulse licensing documentation, complete the policy route, clarify policy precedence and identify checklist controls not covered by the table.

claims.claim: The Viva Pulse admin can control targeted audience surveys through Viva feature access management, including at tenant level.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft documents full Viva Pulse functionality for users with a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Users with a Microsoft Copilot license have access to the full functionality of Viva Pulse to gather real-time feedback from their teams.
claims.fix: Keep the cited statement, then add: 'Microsoft documentation differs: the general Viva Pulse licensing requirements page lists Viva Suite, Viva Workplace Analytics and Employee Feedback, Viva Glint and the Viva Pulse Admin-led Trial for the full premium experience, but does not list Microsoft Copilot. The in-app setup page excludes customization, notification, Viva resources and delegation administration for access through a Microsoft Copilot subscription.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/pulse/get-started/licensing-requirements and https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/pulse/setup-admin-access/set-up-in-app-pulse-experience.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Dashboard integration requires Viva Suite, Viva Workplace Analytics and Employee Feedback, Viva Glint or Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
To integrate Pulse survey results into the Copilot Dashboard, you must have at least one of the following subscription licenses:
- Viva Suite
- Viva Workplace Analytics and Employee Feedback
- Viva Glint
- Microsoft Copilot

claims.claim: Under the Microsoft Copilot subscription, Pulse results for the Copilot impact template are automatically shared to the dashboard.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot (As part of this subscription, Viva Pulse survey results for the Copilot impact template are automatically shared to the Microsoft Copilot Dashboard).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate price or meter for targeted audience surveys is documented at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Pulse targeted audience surveys pricing license meter. Read Measure Microsoft Copilot impact with Viva Pulse, Granular access controls for Viva Pulse and Viva Pulse licensing requirements; no separate targeted-audience price or meter found.

claims.claim: The policy route is Microsoft 365 admin center > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy.
claims.quote: select Viva from the settings menu. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. Select Create a policy. Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off
claims.fix: The printed route stops early on the correct policy page. Extend it to 'Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Viva Pulse > Targeted Audience Surveys > Access setting > Off', and specify in the note to select Everyone under Apply access settings to. Retain the existing caveat about the different route in MC1446805. The policy-creation steps are at https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/control-access-admin-center and the feature name is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/pulse/setup-admin-access/granular-access-controls.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaPulse -FeatureId <FeatureId> -Name <PolicyName> -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone creates a tenant-wide disabling policy.
claims.quote: You can assign one additional policy per feature to the entire tenant by using the -Everyone parameter, which will function as a global default state for that feature across your organization.
claims.fix: Keep the call and FeatureId discovery note. Add to the note: 'The Everyone policy sets the tenant default; policies assigned to individual users or groups take precedence.' This qualification is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/manage-access-policies and https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/control-access-admin-center.

claims.claim: Get-VivaModuleFeature -ModuleId VivaPulse can be used to discover Pulse feature identifiers.
claims.quote:
| Pulse | VivaPulse |
Use the Get-VivaModuleFeature PowerShell cmdlet to get a list of all of the features available in a specific Microsoft 365 app and their associated IDs.

claims.quote: In the Manage tab, go to the Privacy tab. Under the Minimum number of recipients and responses heading go to the Minimum recipients section, where you can select a value between 3 and 25

claims.claim: The Viva Pulse admin role manages the in-app minimum recipient setting.
claims.quote: The Viva Pulse in-app experience can be managed by users with the Viva Pulse admin role. If you're the Viva Pulse admin, you see a Manage tab next to the Home tab in the Viva Pulse header.

claims.claim: The minimum recipient setting accepts values from 3 to 25.
claims.quote: The minimum value allowed is 3 and maximum value allowed is 25.

claims.quote: Searched: Viva Pulse minimum recipients setting API PowerShell Microsoft Graph; "Viva Pulse" "minimum recipients" "API" "PowerShell". Read in-app setup and manage-access-policies; results exposed audit schemas, not an operation setting this threshold.
